fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Install reflective markers along both sides of the driveway to guide responders in low-visibility conditions.
• Clear vegetation along the driveway edges to allow full-width vehicle passage without obstruction.
• Keep a gate or barrier at the driveway entrance unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lockbox if one is present.
• Establish a designated turnaround area near the main residence large enough for fire apparatus to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark any turnaround area clearly so responders can identify it on arrival.
• Trim trees and shrubs that overhang the driveway to maintain a minimum vertical clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back vegetation growing against or immediately adjacent to the detached structure to create separation between plants and the building walls.
• Cut back vegetation growing against or immediately adjacent to the main residence to create separation between plants and the building walls.
• Keep the parking area clear of stored vehicles or equipment that would reduce available staging space for responding units.
• Post the property address at the driveway entrance and again near the main residence to assist responders navigating a long approach.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters closest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that grow directly against the foundation and walls of the structure.
• Separate shrubs and small trees growing beneath large trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Clear dead leaves, needles, and fallen branches from the roof, gutters, and around the base of the structure.
• Thin shrubs and small trees along both sides of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Trim overhanging branches along the full length of the driveway so emergency vehicles can travel without interference.
• Remove or thin dense vegetation at the entrance of the driveway to keep the entry point visible and passable.
• Keep the driveway surface clear of fallen branches and accumulated debris along its full length.
• Create open ground-level gaps between vegetation groupings around the structure so the building is not enclosed by continuous plantings.
• Thin mixed shrubs and trees that grow in dense patches within close range of the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to approaching emergency vehicles.
• Keep the single access route free of parked vehicles, equipment, or stored materials that could block emergency access
